info.name: OnPrintShop GraphQL API
info.description:
Welcome to OnPrintShop's API Documentation. We've designed this document to help developers and OnPrintShop's users fully understand and integrate our API for a seamless and easy deployment.

We've listed all the APIs, their required parameters, and their example requests and responses on the right for easy understanding. The easiest way to start using the OnPrintShop APIs is by clicking the Run in Postman button above. The Postman is a free tool that helps developers run and debug API requests.

Read through the following sections for the integration process.

Getting Started

First, you need to activate the GraphQL API, for this you have to contact our support team. After the successfully activation of GraphQL API you can find your Client Credentials and API End Point URL from the OnPrintShop Admin panel.

Document and API Usage Guidelines

  • Our APIs use the basic HTTP request method: POST
  • You can import and test all our full API collection in the Postman app by clicking on the ' Run in Postman' button.
  • Note: Any requests made using the valid API credentials will affect the real-time data in your OnPrintShop account.
  • Authorization: Bearer
  • All the APIs are provided with their appropriate example requests and responses for successful and failed calls.

Errors and Response codes

While using OnPrintShop's APIs, you may run into some standard response and error codes. The most common ones are listed along with their descriptions as follows:

RESPONSE CODE DESCRIPTION
200 - OK Everything worked as expected, and you'll get a response. Some APIs may respond with an error message if data is invalid.
400 - Bad Request The request was invalid or cannot be otherwise served.
401 - Unauthorized There is some error during validation. You need to check your token or credentials.
404 - Not Found The URI requested is invalid or the resource requested does not exist.
429 - Too Many Requests You have exceeded the API call rate limit.
500, 502, 503, 504 - Server Errors Some server error has occurred. Some APIs may show this due to syntax or parameter errors. Try contacting support if this persists.

API Rate Limiting

To ensure fair usage and optimal performance for all users, our API employs rate limiting. Below is a detailed explanation of the rate limit policy and how it affects your usage.

  • Rate Limit Policy
    • Request Limit: Each user can make up to 120 requests.
    • Time Window: The limit applies to a rolling window of 1 minute.
  • How Rate Limiting Works
    • Counting Requests: Every request you make to the API counts towards your request limit.
    • Time Frame: The rate limit resets every minute. For example, if you start making requests at 10:00:00 AM, your limit will reset at 10:01:00 AM.

Pagination

When you request data from our API, sometimes there might be too much information to handle all at once. To make it easier to view and manage this data, we use a method called "pagination." This means breaking the data into smaller, more manageable chunks or pages.

We are using Limit and Offset based pagination

Key Terms

  • Limit: This is the maximum number of items you want to see on one page.
  • Offset: This tells you where to start from in the list.

How to Use Limit and Offset

For example, you have a large list of items, like 100 records, and you want to view them 10 at a time. Here’s how you can do it:

  • View the First Page
    • Limit: 10 (you want to see 10 items)
    • Offset: 0 (you start from the beginning)
  • View the Second Page
    • Limit: 10 (still want to see 10 items)
    • Offset: 10 (skip the first 10 items and start from the 11th)

Using Total Records

When you request data, the API response also includes the total number of items available. This helps you understand how many pages you can navigate through.

For example, if the total number of records is 100 and you’re viewing 10 items per page:

  • You’ll have 10 pages in total.
  • The first page will have items 1 to 10, the second page will have items 11 to 20, and so on.

Help: Default and Maximum Records Limit

Admin can configure the Max Records Limit (Upto 250) from the Export/API Settings -> Advanced API section of OnPrintShop

  • Default Records Limit
    • If no limit parameter is passed in the API request, the system will return a default of 250 records.
  • Maximum Records Limit
    • The maximum number of records that can be returned in one API call is 250. If a limit parameter greater than 250 is passed, the system will still return a maximum of 250 records.

Authentication Token Generation

By using your Client Credentials you can generate the access token to access the API. For token generation you have to use our Authentication API

API Collection

We offer following API services:

  • Authentication API
    • Generate OAuth2.0 Token
  • Mutations
    • Update Order Status
    • Update Product Stock
  • Queries
    • Customers
    • Customer Address Details
    • Orders
    • Order Details
    • Order Shipment Details
    • Ship To Multiple Address
    • Order and Order Product Statuses
    • Products
    • Product Stocks

item.name: Authentication API
item.description:
Use this API to obtain the authentication token. Copy this token and use it further to validate your API calls. The validity of this token is 24 hr.

Your API keys carry many privileges, so be sure to keep them secure! Do not share your secret token in publicly accessible areas such as GitHub, client-side code, and so forth.

Steps To Use Token:

  • Copy the token received in response.

  • Include 'Authorization: Bearer [yourtokenvalue]' Header in your request

  • That's all! In case of any error, try checking your parameters.

Token Rate Limiting

To ensure fair usage and optimal performance for all users, our API employs token rate limiting. Below is a detailed explanation of the token rate limit policy and how it affects your usage.

  • Token Rate Limit Policy
    • Token Generation Limit: Each user can generate up to 10 tokens.
    • Time Window: The limit applies to a rolling window of 10 minutes.
  • How Token Rate Limiting Works
    • Counting Tokens: Each token generation request counts towards your token limit.
    • Time Frame: The rate limit resets every 10 minutes. For example, if you start generating tokens at 10:00:00 AM, your limit will reset at 10:10:00 AM.
    • Exceeded Limit: If you exceed the 10 token generation requests within ten minutes, you will receive a 429 Token generation limit exceeded, please try again later response. This response indicates that you should wait until the rate limit resets before attempting to generate more tokens.

request.description:
The Product Master Options API provides access to master option configurations including pricing methods, formulas, and presentation settings.

PARAMS REQUIRED DATA TYPE DESCRIPTION EXAMPLE
master_option_id No Int Filter by master option ID 118
limit No Int Maximum number of records to return 10
offset No Int Starting position of records to return 0

Response Fields

FIELD DATA TYPE DESCRIPTION
master_option_id Int Master option ID
title String Option title
description String Option description
production_description String Production description
option_key String Unique option key
pricing_method String Pricing method
status String Option status
sort_order Int Sort order
options_type String Option type
linear_formula String Linear formula
formula String Formula
weight_setting String Weight setting
price_range_lookup String Price range lookup
additional_lookup_details String Additional lookup details
hide_from_calc String Hide from calculator
enable_assoc_qty String Enable associated quantity
allow_price_cal String Allow price calculation
hire_designer_option String Hire designer option
required Int Whether option is required
display_in_calculator Int Display in calculator
option_position String Option position
desc_position Int Description position
display_above_size Int Display above size
presentation_group Int Presentation group
prod_add_opt_export_group_id Int Export group ID
exclude_setup_cost_reorder Int Exclude setup cost on reorder
master_option_tag [Int] Array of master option tag IDs
attributes JSON Option attributes array
external_ref String External reference identifier (nullable, max 255 characters)

The Master Option Tag API provides access to master option tags used for grouping and categorizing options.

PARAMS REQUIRED DATA TYPE DESCRIPTION EXAMPLE
master_option_tag_id No Int Filter by tag ID 1
limit No Int Maximum number of records to return 50
offset No Int Starting position of records to return 0

The Option Group API provides access to product additional option groups used for organizing options in the calculator/frontend.

PARAMS REQUIRED DATA TYPE DESCRIPTION EXAMPLE
prod_add_opt_group_id No Int Filter by option group ID 1
use_for No String Filter by usage type
limit No Int Maximum number of records to return 50
offset No Int Starting position of records to return 0

The Option Formulas API provides access to custom formulas used in product option pricing calculations.

PARAMS REQUIRED DATA TYPE DESCRIPTION EXAMPLE
formula_id No Int Filter by formula ID 1
limit No Int Maximum number of records to return 50
offset No Int Starting position of records to return 0

The Master Option Ranges API provides access to quantity ranges defined for master option attributes, used in range-based pricing.

PARAMS REQUIRED DATA TYPE DESCRIPTION EXAMPLE
range_id No Int Filter by range ID 1
option_id No Int Filter by master option ID 118
limit No Int Maximum number of records to return 50
offset No Int Starting position of records to return 0

The Product Option Prices API provides access to pricing data for master option attributes across quantity ranges.

PARAMS REQUIRED DATA TYPE DESCRIPTION EXAMPLE
attr_id No Int Filter by attribute ID 1
limit No Int Maximum number of records to return 50
offset No Int Starting position of records to return 0

The Product Option Rules API provides access to option visibility rules that control which options/attributes are shown or hidden based on other selections.

PARAMS REQUIRED DATA TYPE DESCRIPTION EXAMPLE
rule_id No Int Filter by rule ID 190
limit No Int Maximum number of records to return 50
offset No Int Starting position of records to return 0

Response Fields

FIELD DATA TYPE DESCRIPTION
rule_id Int Rule ID
rule_name String Rule name
rule_type String Rule type
source_option_ids String Comma-separated source option IDs (positionally maps to source_attribute_ids)
source_attribute_ids String Comma-separated source attribute IDs ("0" means entire option selected)
hide_option_ids String Option IDs to hide
hide_option_attribute_ids String Attribute IDs to hide
status String Rule status
sort_order Int Sort order
comparison_value JSON Comparison value object
disabled_for_admin String Whether rule is disabled for admin

request.description:
The Orders API provides access to all orders along with their respective order product details. Users can filter the results based on the order ID or a specific date range. To get the records either orders_id or from_date is required

PARAMETERS REQUIRED DATA TYPE DESCRIPTION EXAMPLE
orders_id Yes Int This paramter is used to define order id. 1
from_date Yes String This parameter is used to define starting from date. 2024-05-23
to_date No String This paramter is used to define ending to date. 2024-05-24
order_status No String This parameter is used to define status of "order". Pending
customer_id No Int This paramter is used to define customer id. 1
orders_products_id No Int The ID of the ordered product to get specific data 1
order_product_status No Int The Status ID of the order product to get specific data 1
store_id No String Retrieve orders based on a store ID (optional). The store ID can follow either of the patterns:
1. Store and Child Store Filter (e.g., 2): This will filter orders for the store with ID 2 and its child stores, if any.
2. Store Specific Filter (e.g., 2_0): The underscore zero indicates that orders should be filtered for only the store with ID 2.		 1
order_type No Enum The order_type parameter in API allows users to filter the records based on the order ID. It supports two values: lt (less than) and gt (greater than).

Less Than (lt)
When a user sets order_type=lt and provides an order_id value, the API will return records where the order ID is less than the specified order_id. This is useful for retrieving orders that were placed before a certain order. For example, if a user filters by order_id=3 and sets order_type=lt, the API will return all orders with an ID less than 3 (e.g., 1, 2).

Greater Than (gt)
When a user sets order_type=gt and provides an order_id value, the API will return records where the order ID is greater than the specified order_id. This is useful for retrieving orders that were placed after a certain order. For example, if a user filters by order_id=3 and sets order_type=gt, the API will return all orders with an ID greater than 3 (e.g., 4, 5, 6).		 lt / gt
limit No Int This paramter specifies the maximum number of records to return in a single API call. 50
offset No Int This paramter specifies the starting position of the records to return. 0

request.description:
This API allows you to retrieve detailed information about all customers.

PARAMETERS REQUIRED DATA TYPE DESCRIPTION EXAMPLE
email No String This paramter is used to filter the records by Email Id BrianFarrell@test.com
from_date Yes String This parameter is used to define starting from date. 2024-05-21
to_date No String This paramter is used to define ending to date. 2024-05-21
date_type No Enum This parameter allows you to specify whether you want to see data based on login dates or registration dates.

If you do not provide a date_type parameter, the API will default to returning records filtered by the user's registration date.		 login / registration
limit No Int This paramter specifies the maximum number of records to return in a single API. 50
offset No Int This paramter specifies the starting position of the records to return. 0

Response Fields

FIELD DATA TYPE DESCRIPTION
userid Int Customer user ID
user_type String Store type of the customer
customers_name String Full name of the customer
customers_first_name String First name
customers_last_name String Last name
customers_company String Company name
customers_telephone String Telephone number
customers_email_address String Email address
customers_corporate_name String Corporate/franchise store name (nullable)
customers_status String Account status (Active/Inactive)
customers_payon_enable Boolean Whether pay-on-account is enabled
customers_pay_limit Int Pay-on-account credit limit
customers_balance_amount Int Current balance amount
customers_department_name String Department name (nullable)

customers_register_date String Registration date
customers_username String Username (nullable)
customers_secondary_emails String Secondary email addresses (nullable)
reward_points Int Reward points balance
external_ref String External reference identifier for third-party system integration (nullable, max 255 characters)
address_detail Array List of customer addresses
totalCustomers Int Total count of customers matching the query

PARAMS REQUIRED DATA TYPE DESCRIPTION EXAMPLE
rule_id No* Int Rule ID – required only for update/delete 213
rule_name Yes String Rule name "TEST rule"
rule_type Yes String Rule type (See Rule Type Legend) "param_additional_option_based"
source_option_ids Conditional String Comma-separated option IDs. Required if rule_type is not "Size-Quantity based". Positionally maps to source_attribute_ids. "151,237,456"
source_attribute_ids Conditional String Comma-separated attribute IDs. Required if rule_type is not "Size-Quantity based". Use "0" to select entire option. "316,0,0"
hide_option_ids No String Comma-separated master option IDs to completely hide when rule matches. Hides the entire option (all its attributes become invisible). "45,67"
hide_option_attribute_ids No String Comma-separated attribute IDs to hide when rule matches. Hides specific attributes within options — the parent option remains visible with remaining attributes. "391,1112,1113"
status No Int Rule status (0 = inactive, 1 = active). Inactive rules are ignored during evaluation. 0
custom_param Yes String Custom parameter (See Custom Param Legend) "area"
rules_quantity_select Conditional Int Required if rule_type = Size-Quantity based (See Quantity Select Legend) 0
rules_quantity Conditional Int Required if rules_quantity_select = 1 (Specific Quantity) 1
rules_quantity_to Conditional Int Required if rules_quantity_select = 1 (Specific Quantity) 100
custom_param_val Conditional Float Required if custom_param is NOT "size" 1
custom_param_val_to Conditional Float Required if custom_param is NOT "size" 100
custom_param_width Conditional Float Required if custom_param = "size" 1
custom_param_width_to Conditional Float Required if custom_param = "size" 100
custom_param_height Conditional Float Required if custom_param = "size" 1
custom_param_height_to Conditional Float Required if custom_param = "size" 100
sort_order No Int Evaluation priority. Rules are evaluated in ascending sort_order. Lower values execute first. When multiple rules match, later rules (higher sort_order) override earlier ones. 99999
hide_size_ids No String Comma-separated size IDs to hide when rule matches ""
opt_textbox_conditions No Array Textbox conditions array (See structure below) [ {…} ]
condition No String AND / OR relation between different source option attributes "AND"
disabled_for_admin No Int Disable rule on admin side (0 = enabled, 1 = disabled for admin) 0
delete No Int Use 1 to delete rule 0

Source Option/Attribute Mapping

source_option_ids and source_attribute_ids are positionally mapped comma-separated strings:

  • 1st value in source_option_ids pairs with 1st value in source_attribute_ids
  • Use "0" as attribute ID to select the entire option (all attributes)

Example: Selecting option 123 with attributes 456 and 987, plus entire option 456:

"source_option_ids": "123,123,456",
"source_attribute_ids": "456,987,0"

hide_option_ids vs hide_option_attribute_ids

These two fields control what gets hidden when the rule condition is met:

Field Scope Behavior
hide_option_ids Entire option Hides the complete option including all its attributes. The option becomes invisible to the user.
hide_option_attribute_ids Specific attributes Hides individual attributes within an option. The parent option remains visible with its remaining (non-hidden) attributes.

Use hide_option_ids when:

  • You want to completely remove an option from the user's view
  • Example: Hide "Lamination" option entirely when paper type is "Recycled"

Use hide_option_attribute_ids when:

  • You want to remove specific choices within an option but keep the option visible
  • Example: Hide "Glossy" and "Matte" finishes (attributes) from the "Finish" option, but keep "Satin" available

Both can be used together in the same rule to hide entire options AND specific attributes from other options simultaneously.

sort_order — Rule Evaluation Priority

Rules are evaluated in ascending sort_order (lowest first).

Behavior Description
Evaluation order Rules with lower sort_order are evaluated first
Conflict resolution When multiple rules match the same condition, the rule with the higher sort_order (evaluated later) takes precedence
Default value 99999 (evaluated last)
Recommended practice Use increments of 10 (10, 20, 30…) to allow inserting rules between existing ones

Example:

  • Rule A (sort_order: 10) — hides attribute 391
  • Rule B (sort_order: 20) — hides attributes 391, 1112, 1113

If both rules match, Rule B's hide list takes effect because it has a higher sort_order.

Textbox Condition Object Structure

Each object inside opt_textbox_conditions must follow this structure:

KEY REQUIRED DATA TYPE DESCRIPTION EXAMPLE
opt_key Yes String Option-attribute key in format optionId_attributeId (use _0 for entire option) "237_0"
opt_comparison Yes String Comparison operator (See Comparison Operators) "<=>"
opt_val_from Conditional Float Required for all operators. The comparison value (or range start for <=>) 1
opt_val_to Conditional Float Required only for <=> (Between). The range end value. 100

Comparison Operators

Used in opt_textbox_conditions to define value-based conditions on textbox options:

Operator Name Description Required Fields Example
= Equal To Matches when the textbox value equals opt_val_from exactly opt_val_from Value = 5
>= Greater Or Equal To Matches when the textbox value is greater than or equal to opt_val_from opt_val_from Value >= 10
<= Less Or Equal To Matches when the textbox value is less than or equal to opt_val_from opt_val_from Value <= 50
<=> Between Matches when the textbox value falls within the range opt_val_from to opt_val_to (inclusive) opt_val_from, opt_val_to 1 <= Value <= 100

Note: If opt_comparison is <=> and either opt_val_from or opt_val_to is missing/empty, the condition for that source option attribute is skipped (removed from evaluation).

This API is used to set product SKU variants. You can setup SKU for products based on two different methods. SKU will be considered for only one method at a time.

  • Size Wise : SKU can be defined based on product sizes.
  • Size Option Wise : SKU can be defined for each combination of Size and Option attributes.

Remaining sizes or combinations that are not provided will be auto-filled with blank SKU entries. Switching between methods will remove previous method's records automatically.

To set the main product SKU, use the setProduct mutation with the main_sku field.

PARAMS REQUIRED DATA TYPE DESCRIPTION EXAMPLE
products_id Yes Int Product ID 336
sku_type Conditional String SKU method. Required for insert/update. Possible Values: size_wise, size_option_wise "size_wise"
size_id Conditional Int Product size ID. Required for insert/update. 101
prod_add_opt_ids Conditional String Comma-separated option IDs. Required for size_option_wise****. "8021,8022"
attribute_ids Conditional String Comma-separated attribute IDs (one per option, same order). Required for size_option_wise****. Count must match prod_add_opt_ids. "13868,13871"
sku Conditional String SKU value (can be empty). Required for insert/update. "SKU-BLK-LG-001"
delete Conditional Int Set 1 to delete all variant SKUs for the product. Only products_id needed. 1

Size Option Wise — Matrix Example

When using size_option_wise, each entry represents one cell in the matrix of Sizes × Option Attribute Combinations.

Setup:

  • Product has 2 sizes: Small (101), Large (102)
  • 2 options selected: Color (8021), Material (8022)
  • Color attributes: Black (13868), White (13869)
  • Material attributes: Cotton (13871), Polyester (13872)

How prod_add_opt_ids and attribute_ids work:

prod_add_opt_ids stays the same for all entries — it's the selected options: "8021,8022"

attribute_ids changes per entry — one attribute per option in the same order:

Size Color (8021) Material (8022) attribute_ids
Small (101) Black (13868) Cotton (13871) "13868,13871"
Small (101) Black (13868) Polyester (13872) "13868,13872"
Small (101) White (13869) Cotton (13871) "13869,13871"
Small (101) White (13869) Polyester (13872) "13869,13872"
Large (102) Black (13868) Cotton (13871) "13868,13871"
Large (102) Black (13868) Polyester (13872) "13868,13872"
Large (102) White (13869) Cotton (13871) "13869,13871"
Large (102) White (13869) Polyester (13872) "13869,13872"

Total entries = Sizes (2) × Color attrs (2) × Material attrs (2) = 8

You only need to send entries where you want to set a SKU value. Remaining combinations will be auto-filled with blank SKU.

markup_title is required on insert Markup Title is required.

Legends

Markup Type (markup_type)

Value Meaning
0 Fixed — single percentage applied to all
1 Dynamic — tiered brackets based on price or quantity

Markup Lookup (markup_by)

Value Meaning
0 Price — brackets based on product price
1 Quantity — brackets based on order quantity

Applied On (appliedon)

Value Meaning
0 Base Price
1 Vendor Price
